findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded directly in the Lambda function's environment variables in source control. Anyone with read access to the repo, the Lambda console, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve and reuse these static credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which here contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in plaintext by any principal with basic Lambda read permissions, with no customer-managed key policy to constrain access.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a runtime that has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, easing data exfiltration if the function is compromised.
